statement.p: Compute the flux of \vec F = 2 x\vec i + 2 y\vec j + 3 z\vec k over the quarter cylinder S given by x^2+y^2=25, 0\leq x\leq 5, 0\leq y\leq 5, 0\leq z\leq 5, oriented outward.

static.solution:
\vec k-component of \vec F does not contribute to the flux as it is perpendicular to the surface. The vector field 2 x\vec i + 2 y\vec j is everywhere perpendicular to S and has constant magnitude ||(2 x)^2+(2 y)^2|| = 2 on the surface S. Thus \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A =\int_S 2(x\vec i +y\vec j)\cdot d\vec A =2\cdot \hbox{Area of }S = 2\frac{25 \pi}{2} = 25\,\pi.
Alternatively, the flux can be computed by integrating with respect to x and z, treating y as a function of x and z. A parameterization of S is given by y=\sqrt{25-x^2}, 0\leq x\leq 5, 0\leq y\leq 5, 0\leq z\leq 5. Thus, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{5}\int_0^{5}(2 x\vec i + 2 \sqrt{1-x^2}\vec j+ 3 z\vec k) \cdot(-y_x\vec i + \vec j- y_z \vec k)\,dx\,dz = \int_0^{5}\int_0^{5}(2 x\vec i+ 2 \sqrt{1-x^2}\vec j+ 3 z\vec k) \cdot\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{25 -x^2}}\vec i +\vec j + 0\vec k\right)\,dx\,dz = \int_0^{5}\int_0^{5}\left(2\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{25-x^2}} + 2 \sqrt{25 -x^2}\right)\,dx\,dz = 2 \int_0^{5}\int_0^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{25-x^2}}\,dx\,dz = 50\cdot \arcsin \frac{x}{5}\bigg|_0^{5} = 25\,\pi.
